articles.title: Mirror, Mirror, in the Tank: Octopuses Learn to Use Reflections to Hunt
articles.summary: In a first for invertebrates, octopuses learned to use a mirror to locate hidden prey. Dartmouth researchers trained them to interpret a virtual crab's reflection, then turn around to claim a real reward. The study suggests these alien-like minds may build internal maps of their world.

articles.title: A Pocket-Sized X-Ray Telescope Could Reveal the Moon's Elemental Secrets
articles.summary: A compact X-ray telescope, weighing under 10 kg, could create the first complete chemical map of the lunar surface. Simulations show it could map five key elements in two years, or faster with a small array. The data would transform our understanding of the Moon's geological history.

articles.title: Harnessing Fire Tornadoes: A Faster, Greener Way to Battle Oil Spills
articles.summary: In a groundbreaking large-scale study, researchers created 17-foot fire whirls that burn crude oil nearly twice as fast as conventional methods, with dramatically lower emissions. The spinning vortex could revolutionize oil spill response, protecting coastlines and marine life more effectively.
